# TTM-HumanPref: G-Clef FluxAudio-S checkpoint (ICME 2026 ATTM Grand Challenge)

Final submitted checkpoint of **Team G-Clef** for the Efficiency track of the [ICME 2026 Academic Text-to-Music Grand Challenge](https://ntu-musicailab.github.io/ICME26-ATTM-Grand-Challenge/).

A ~120M-parameter FluxAudio-S rectified-flow model, trained from scratch on the challenge's CC-licensed instrumental MTG-Jamendo subset, then refined with human-preference reward conditioning, expert iteration, and a short CRPO preference fine-tune.

- **Paper:** [Improving Text-to-Music Generation with Human Preference Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21670)
- **Code:** [github.com/yonghyunk1m/TTM-HumanPref](https://github.com/yonghyunk1m/TTM-HumanPref)
- **Demo:** [TTM-HumanPref Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/yonghyunk1m/TTM-HumanPref)

## Files

| File | Size | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gclef_crpoA_fluxaudio_s.pt` | 483 MB | Final CRPO-A checkpoint, used for both submissions |

SHA-256: `0cfb8295fbd695a99c7a2599363a465fdc28a94f39c8d43faf7487461e5e15f2`

This file is identical to the asset of the GitHub release [`v1.0-icme2026`](https://github.com/yonghyunk1m/TTM-HumanPref/releases/tag/v1.0-icme2026).

## Usage

Inference runs through the code repository, on top of the official challenge baseline. See the [GitHub README](https://github.com/yonghyunk1m/TTM-HumanPref) for setup.

```bash
python run.py download-weights          # fetches this checkpoint and verifies its SHA-256
python run.py reproduce --seed 42       # Submission 1
python run.py reproduce --seed 55       # Submission 2
```

Both submissions come from this single checkpoint and differ only in the generation seed. Inference uses joint classifier-free guidance on text and reward, 25 Euler steps, and the prompt prefix `"high quality instrumental music, "`.

## Intended use and limitations

Research and non-commercial use. The model generates instrumental music only (~10 s, 44.1 kHz) and was trained on a limited instrumental subset of MTG-Jamendo, so its stylistic coverage reflects that data.

The model weights are released under [CC BY-NC 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/) (see `LICENSE`). The code in the GitHub repository is MIT.

--- license: apache-2.0 language: - en - zh library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: audio-text-to-text tags: - music - music-understanding - audio - audio-language-model - moss - moss-music - lyrics-asr - music-captioning - chord-recognition --- # MOSS-Music

English | 简体中文

**MOSS-Music** is an open-source **music understanding model** from [MOSI.AI](https://mosi.cn/#hero), the [OpenMOSS team](https://www.open-moss.com/), and [Shanghai Innovation Institute](https://www.sii.edu.cn/). Built on the same audio backbone as [MOSS-Audio](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Audio), MOSS-Music is further specialised on music via dedicated continual pre-training and supervised fine-tuning — targeting **musical captioning, lyrics ASR, structural analysis, chord / key / tempo reasoning, and long-form musical question answering**. In this release, we provide **two 8B models**: **MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct** and **MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking**. The Instruct variant is optimised for direct instruction following on musical prompts, while the Thinking variant provides stronger chain-of-thought reasoning for musical analysis. ## News * 2026.05.01: 🎉🎉🎉 We have released [MOSS-Music](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Music). * 2026.05.01: 🎉🎉🎉 We have released [MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline](https://github.com/wx9songs/MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline) for large-scale music data annotation and processing. ## Contents - [Introduction](#introduction) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [DeepStack Cross-Layer Feature Injection](#deepstack-cross-layer-feature-injection) - [Time-Aware Representation](#time-aware-representation) - [Released Models](#released-models) - [Music Data Pipeline](#music-data-pipeline) - [Evaluation](#evaluation) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Environment Setup](#environment-setup) - [SGLang Serving](#sglang-serving) - [Gradio App](#gradio-app) - [More Information](#more-information) - [LICENSE](#license) - [Citation](#citation) ## Introduction Music is not just audio plus lyrics — understanding it requires perceiving harmonic structure, rhythm, timbre, instrumentation, performance nuance, and the textual content of the lyrics, and reasoning about them jointly across time. **MOSS-Music** is built to unify these capabilities within a single model. - **Lyrics ASR & time-aligned transcription**: Accurate singing ASR with sentence- and word-level timestamps, robust to backing tracks. - **Musical captioning & tagging**: Natural-language descriptions of mood, genre, instrumentation, production style, and emotional trajectory. - **Key / tempo / chord reasoning**: Identifies musical key, beats, downbeats, and chord progressions, including timestamped chord transcription. - **Structural analysis**: Segments a song into intro / verse / chorus / bridge / outro and reasons about repetition and contrast. - **Instrument & voice recognition**: Identifies prominent instruments and singing voices (solo / chorus, gender, register). - **Musical QA and long-form analysis**: Open-ended question answering grounded in a full track, including chain-of-thought reasoning in the *Thinking* variant.

## Model Architecture MOSS-Music inherits the MOSS-Audio modular design, comprising three components: an audio encoder, a modality adapter, and a large language model. Raw audio is first encoded by **MOSS-Audio-Encoder** into continuous temporal representations at **12.5 Hz**, which are then projected into the language model's embedding space through the adapter and finally consumed by the LLM for auto-regressive text generation. Rather than relying on off-the-shelf audio frontends, we train a dedicated encoder from scratch to obtain more robust acoustic representations, tighter temporal alignment, and better extensibility across musical styles, singing, and non-speech acoustic content. ### DeepStack Cross-Layer Feature Injection Using only the encoder's top-layer features tends to lose low-level prosody, transient events, and local time-frequency structure. To address this, we adopt a **DeepStack**-inspired cross-layer injection module between the encoder and the language model: in addition to the encoder's final-layer output, features from earlier and intermediate layers are selected, independently projected, and injected into the language model's early layers, preserving multi-granularity information from low-level acoustic details to high-level semantic abstractions. This design is especially well-suited for music understanding, as it helps retain rhythm, timbre, transients, and instrumental texture — information that a single high-level representation cannot fully capture, yet is critical for chord recognition, structural analysis, and nuanced musical description. ### Time-Aware Representation Time is a critical dimension in music understanding. To enhance explicit temporal awareness, we adopt a **time-marker insertion** strategy during pre-training: explicit time tokens are inserted between audio frame representations at fixed time intervals to indicate temporal positions. This design enables the model to learn "what happened when" within a unified text generation framework, naturally supporting timestamped lyrics ASR, beat / downbeat localisation, section boundary detection, and long-song retrospective QA. Building on the MOSS-Audio backbone, MOSS-Music is further enhanced through: - **continual pre-training** on a large, diverse music corpus produced by the data annotation and processing pipeline [`MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline`](https://github.com/wx9songs/MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline), with an emphasis on singing, lyrics, and full-song coverage; - **supervised fine-tuning (SFT)** on music-centric instruction data covering captioning, lyrics ASR, chord / key / structural analysis, and long-form musical QA; - additional **reasoning tuning** for the *Thinking* variant. ## Released Models | Model | Audio Encoder | LLM Backbone | Total Size | Hugging Face | ModelScope | |---|---|---|---:|---|---| | **MOSS‑Music‑8B‑Instruct** | MOSS-Audio-Encoder | Qwen3-8B | ~9.1B | [![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/Huggingface-Model-orange?logo=huggingface)](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct) | [![ModelScope](https://img.shields.io/badge/ModelScope-Model-624AFF)](https://modelscope.cn/models/openmoss/MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct) | | **MOSS‑Music‑8B‑Thinking** | MOSS-Audio-Encoder | Qwen3-8B | ~9.1B | [![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/Huggingface-Model-orange?logo=huggingface)](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking) | [![ModelScope](https://img.shields.io/badge/ModelScope-Model-624AFF)](https://modelscope.cn/models/openmoss/MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking) | > Smaller (4B) variants and additional sizes may follow. Stay tuned! ## Music Data Pipeline The training data used by MOSS-Music is produced by an end-to-end pipeline that goes from raw audio to chat-formatted training samples. That pipeline is available at [`MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline`](https://github.com/wx9songs/MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline), which hosts duration detection, MIR feature extraction, song-structure segmentation, lyrics ASR, metadata cleanup, and ALM-driven caption / query generation with models such as Qwen3-Omni, MusicFlamingo, and other audio-language models.

## Evaluation We evaluate MOSS-Music on a diverse suite of public music understanding benchmarks. Key results: - **Music QA and understanding**: **MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct** achieves **80.38** average accuracy across **8 public music QA benchmarks** (excluding the three NSynth note-recognition tracks), ranking first among all compared models in our current evaluation set. - **Music captioning**: In our preliminary **GPT-5.4-as-a-Judge** evaluation, the MOSS-Music series leads both caption benchmarks, with `MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking` reaching **4.53** on `MusicCaps` and `MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct` reaching **4.58** on `SDD`. - **Lyrics ASR for singing voice**: **MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking** achieves the best average lyrics recognition error across `MUSDB18`, `MIR-1K` and `Opencpop` (**15.88%** avg WER/CER), clearly ahead of all compared audio-language baselines including `Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview`, `MusicFlamingo` and `Qwen3-Omni`. Detailed timestamped-ASR results will be released in a later update. - **Chord transcription**: MOSS-Music supports chord transcription, including timestamped chord transcription for harmonic analysis, accompaniment reference, and related downstream use cases. Detailed benchmark results will be released in a later update.

The commands below are enough for local inference. #### Recommended setup ```bash git clone https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Music.git cd MOSS-Music conda create -n moss-music python=3.12 -y conda activate moss-music conda install -c conda-forge "ffmpeg=7" -y pip install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 -e ".[torch-runtime]" ``` #### Optional: FlashAttention 2 If your GPU supports FlashAttention 2, you can replace the last install command with: ```bash pip install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 -e ".[torch-runtime,flash-attn]" ``` ### SGLang Serving > [!IMPORTANT] > To achieve the best generation quality and fully leverage the model's capabilities, we > **strongly recommend using SGLang Serving for inference**. --- license: apache-2.0 language: - en - zh library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: audio-text-to-text tags: - music - music-understanding - audio - audio-language-model - moss - moss-music - lyrics-asr - music-captioning - chord-recognition --- # MOSS-Music

English | 简体中文

**MOSS-Music** is an open-source **music understanding model** from [MOSI.AI](https://mosi.cn/#hero), the [OpenMOSS team](https://www.open-moss.com/), and [Shanghai Innovation Institute](https://www.sii.edu.cn/). Built on the same audio backbone as [MOSS-Audio](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Audio), MOSS-Music is further specialised on music via dedicated continual pre-training and supervised fine-tuning — targeting **musical captioning, lyrics ASR, structural analysis, chord / key / tempo reasoning, and long-form musical question answering**. In this release, we provide **two 8B models**: **MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct** and **MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking**. The Instruct variant is optimised for direct instruction following on musical prompts, while the Thinking variant provides stronger chain-of-thought reasoning for musical analysis. ## News * 2026.05.01: 🎉🎉🎉 We have released [MOSS-Music](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Music). * 2026.05.01: 🎉🎉🎉 We have released [MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline](https://github.com/wx9songs/MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline) for large-scale music data annotation and processing. ## Contents - [Introduction](#introduction) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [DeepStack Cross-Layer Feature Injection](#deepstack-cross-layer-feature-injection) - [Time-Aware Representation](#time-aware-representation) - [Released Models](#released-models) - [Music Data Pipeline](#music-data-pipeline) - [Evaluation](#evaluation) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Environment Setup](#environment-setup) - [SGLang Serving](#sglang-serving) - [Gradio App](#gradio-app) - [More Information](#more-information) - [LICENSE](#license) - [Citation](#citation) ## Introduction Music is not just audio plus lyrics — understanding it requires perceiving harmonic structure, rhythm, timbre, instrumentation, performance nuance, and the textual content of the lyrics, and reasoning about them jointly across time. **MOSS-Music** is built to unify these capabilities within a single model. - **Lyrics ASR & time-aligned transcription**: Accurate singing ASR with sentence- and word-level timestamps, robust to backing tracks. - **Musical captioning & tagging**: Natural-language descriptions of mood, genre, instrumentation, production style, and emotional trajectory. - **Key / tempo / chord reasoning**: Identifies musical key, beats, downbeats, and chord progressions, including timestamped chord transcription. - **Structural analysis**: Segments a song into intro / verse / chorus / bridge / outro and reasons about repetition and contrast. - **Instrument & voice recognition**: Identifies prominent instruments and singing voices (solo / chorus, gender, register). - **Musical QA and long-form analysis**: Open-ended question answering grounded in a full track, including chain-of-thought reasoning in the *Thinking* variant.

## Model Architecture MOSS-Music inherits the MOSS-Audio modular design, comprising three components: an audio encoder, a modality adapter, and a large language model. Raw audio is first encoded by **MOSS-Audio-Encoder** into continuous temporal representations at **12.5 Hz**, which are then projected into the language model's embedding space through the adapter and finally consumed by the LLM for auto-regressive text generation. Rather than relying on off-the-shelf audio frontends, we train a dedicated encoder from scratch to obtain more robust acoustic representations, tighter temporal alignment, and better extensibility across musical styles, singing, and non-speech acoustic content. ### DeepStack Cross-Layer Feature Injection Using only the encoder's top-layer features tends to lose low-level prosody, transient events, and local time-frequency structure. To address this, we adopt a **DeepStack**-inspired cross-layer injection module between the encoder and the language model: in addition to the encoder's final-layer output, features from earlier and intermediate layers are selected, independently projected, and injected into the language model's early layers, preserving multi-granularity information from low-level acoustic details to high-level semantic abstractions. This design is especially well-suited for music understanding, as it helps retain rhythm, timbre, transients, and instrumental texture — information that a single high-level representation cannot fully capture, yet is critical for chord recognition, structural analysis, and nuanced musical description. ### Time-Aware Representation Time is a critical dimension in music understanding. To enhance explicit temporal awareness, we adopt a **time-marker insertion** strategy during pre-training: explicit time tokens are inserted between audio frame representations at fixed time intervals to indicate temporal positions. This design enables the model to learn "what happened when" within a unified text generation framework, naturally supporting timestamped lyrics ASR, beat / downbeat localisation, section boundary detection, and long-song retrospective QA. Building on the MOSS-Audio backbone, MOSS-Music is further enhanced through: - **continual pre-training** on a large, diverse music corpus produced by the data annotation and processing pipeline [`MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline`](https://github.com/wx9songs/MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline), with an emphasis on singing, lyrics, and full-song coverage; - **supervised fine-tuning (SFT)** on music-centric instruction data covering captioning, lyrics ASR, chord / key / structural analysis, and long-form musical QA; - additional **reasoning tuning** for the *Thinking* variant. ## Released Models | Model | Audio Encoder | LLM Backbone | Total Size | Hugging Face | ModelScope | |---|---|---|---:|---|---| | **MOSS‑Music‑8B‑Instruct** | MOSS-Audio-Encoder | Qwen3-8B | ~9.1B | [![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/Huggingface-Model-orange?logo=huggingface)](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct) | [![ModelScope](https://img.shields.io/badge/ModelScope-Model-624AFF)](https://modelscope.cn/models/openmoss/MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct) | | **MOSS‑Music‑8B‑Thinking** | MOSS-Audio-Encoder | Qwen3-8B | ~9.1B | [![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/Huggingface-Model-orange?logo=huggingface)](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking) | [![ModelScope](https://img.shields.io/badge/ModelScope-Model-624AFF)](https://modelscope.cn/models/openmoss/MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking) | > Smaller (4B) variants and additional sizes may follow. Stay tuned! ## Music Data Pipeline The training data used by MOSS-Music is produced by an end-to-end pipeline that goes from raw audio to chat-formatted training samples. That pipeline is available at [`MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline`](https://github.com/wx9songs/MOSS-Music-Data-Pipeline), which hosts duration detection, MIR feature extraction, song-structure segmentation, lyrics ASR, metadata cleanup, and ALM-driven caption / query generation with models such as Qwen3-Omni, MusicFlamingo, and other audio-language models.

## Evaluation We evaluate MOSS-Music on a diverse suite of public music understanding benchmarks. Key results: - **Music QA and understanding**: **MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct** achieves **80.38** average accuracy across **8 public music QA benchmarks** (excluding the three NSynth note-recognition tracks), ranking first among all compared models in our current evaluation set. - **Music captioning**: In our preliminary **GPT-5.4-as-a-Judge** evaluation, the MOSS-Music series leads both caption benchmarks, with `MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking` reaching **4.53** on `MusicCaps` and `MOSS-Music-8B-Instruct` reaching **4.58** on `SDD`. - **Lyrics ASR for singing voice**: **MOSS-Music-8B-Thinking** achieves the best average lyrics recognition error across `MUSDB18`, `MIR-1K` and `Opencpop` (**15.88%** avg WER/CER), clearly ahead of all compared audio-language baselines including `Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview`, `MusicFlamingo` and `Qwen3-Omni`. Detailed timestamped-ASR results will be released in a later update. - **Chord transcription**: MOSS-Music supports chord transcription, including timestamped chord transcription for harmonic analysis, accompaniment reference, and related downstream use cases. Detailed benchmark results will be released in a later update.

Lure 0.6B

Expressive voice cloning in 0.6B parameters. It laughs, sighs, breaks and whispers where you tell it to.
Research preview · English · 0.6B parameters · 24 kHz

[![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live%20demo-e8590c?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/smirki/lure-tts) [![Lure Turbo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lure%20Turbo-7048e8?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/Tesslate/Lure-TTS-Turbo) [![Engine](https://img.shields.io/badge/Engine-1c7ed6?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts) [![Training code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Training%20code-2f9e44?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/smirki/lure-train)
> [!WARNING] > **Research preview.** Weights, behaviour and this card can change between releases. Pin a revision if you build on it. ## Overview Lure is a 0.6B text-to-speech model for English. Give it a few seconds of a voice and the transcript of that clip, and it reads new text in that voice. A sound written inline, like `(sigh)` or `(sharp inhale)`, is performed at that spot instead of read out. A short acting note, like `"Hushed and shaking, close to tears."`, changes how the line is played. Most open models in its class are 1.5B to 35B parameters. On the public English benchmarks below, Lure's word accuracy sits alongside models three to sixty times its size, and its naturalness score (UTMOS) is the highest in the table. It runs faster than real time on a MacBook, and a single 24 GB GPU streams 8 voices at once. Lure Turbo is the same voice with a faster decoding head. It predicts the 15 fine audio codes of each frame in 3 passes instead of 15, so the per-frame decode step is about 3.4x faster, and its benchmark scores match Lure's. See [Speed](#speed). | | | |---|---| | **Parameters** | 0.6B | | **Language** | English only | | **Output** | 24 kHz mono, streaming | | **Codec** | 12.5 Hz, 16 codebooks (Qwen3-TTS 12Hz format) | | **Cloning** | zero-shot, 3 to 12 s reference plus its transcript | | **Sounds** | inline tags in round brackets, 36 supported | | **Direction** | optional free-text acting note | ## Speed Lure streams audio while it generates. RTF is generation time divided by audio length, so lower is faster. All numbers come from the [lure-tts](https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts) engine with the cuda backend in bf16. **H100** | Model | Streams | ms per frame | RTF | |---|---|---|---| | Lure | 1 | 18.4 | 0.23 | | Lure | 8 | 19.6 | 0.25 | | Lure Turbo | 1 | **11.4** | **0.14** | | Lure Turbo | 8 | 12.4 | 0.15 | **24 GB GPU** | Model | 1 stream | 8 streams, total | |---|---|---| | Lure | 28.8 frames/s (2.3x real time) | 219 frames/s (17x real time) | | Lure Turbo | **50.6 frames/s (4.0x real time)** | **374 frames/s (30x real time)** | ## Benchmarks

We ran Lure and Lure Turbo with each benchmark's official scripts, one take per line and default sampling. The other rows are the numbers their developers published. The best value in each column is in bold. | Model | Size | Seed-TTS WER ↓ | Seed-TTS SIM ↑ | LibriSpeech-PC SIM ↑ | LibriSpeech-PC UTMOS ↑ | VDB SIM ↑ | CV3 emotion % ↑ | RTF ↓ | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Lure** | 0.6B | 1.51 | 0.653 | 0.638 | **4.43** | **0.81** | 73.3 | 0.230 | | **Lure Turbo** | 0.6B | 1.59 | 0.654 | 0.641 | 4.38 | **0.81** | 73.3 | 0.140 | | Fish S2 Pro | 5B | **0.99** | – | – | – | – | – | 0.195 | | Qwen3-TTS 0.6B | 0.6B | 1.32 | – | – | – | – | – | – | | Fish Drama 3 | 35B MoE | 1.54 | 0.640 | 0.605 | 4.31 | – | – | **0.131** | | Ming 3.0 0.5B | ~1B | 1.58 | 0.691 | – | – | – | – | – | | FireRedTTS3 | 1.7B+ | 1.64 | **0.772** | – | – | – | – | – | | VoxCPM2 | 2B | 1.84 | 0.753 | – | – | 0.70 | – | – | | F5-TTS | – | 2.00 | 0.670 | – | – | – | 64.7 | – | | CosyVoice3 | – | 2.22 | 0.720 | 0.694 | 4.28 | – | – | – | | Breeze TTS 2 | 3B | – | – | – | – | 0.67 | – | 0.320 | | dots.tts | 2B | – | 0.770 | – | – | – | – | – | | Ming Tiny | 7.9B MoE | – | 0.728 | – | – | – | 74.0 | – | | IndexTTS2 | 1.5B | – | 0.706 | – | – | – | – | – | | OmniVoice | 0.6B | – | – | **0.729** | 4.28 | – | – | – | | Qwen3-TTS | 0.6B-1.7B | – | – | 0.704 | 4.41 | – | – | – | | Real recordings | – | – | – | – | 4.10 | – | – | – | | Inworld TTS-2 | – | – | – | – | – | 0.71 | – | – | | MiMo-v2.5 | – | – | – | – | – | 0.66 | – | – | | Qwen-Audio 3.0+ | – | – | – | – | – | 0.65 | – | – | | StepAudio 2.5 | – | – | – | – | – | 0.64 | – | – | | CosyVoice3 1.5B +DiffRO-EMO | 1.5B | – | – | – | – | – | **77.7** | – | | Ming 0.5B | ~1B | – | – | – | – | – | 72.3 | – | | CosyVoice3 0.5B | 0.5B | – | – | – | – | – | 66.3 | – | | CosyVoice3 1.5B | 1.5B | – | – | – | – | – | 63.0 | – | | Higgs TTS 3 | 4B | – | – | – | – | – | – | 0.147 | ## Quick start ### lure-tts (recommended: streaming, Turbo, Mac / NVIDIA / CPU) ```bash git clone https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts && cd lure-tts hf download Tesslate/Lure-TTS-0.6B --local-dir models/lure pip install ./backends/mlx ".[server]" # Mac; see the repo for NVIDIA and the C++ build ``` ```python from lure_tts import Lure tts = Lure.load("models/lure") voice = tts.make_voice("reference.wav", "Transcript of the reference clip.", name="me") tts.speak("Wait, you're staying? (sharp inhale) Since when?", voice, instruct="Sudden, bright shock, then a caught breath.", out="out.wav") for pcm in tts.stream("(sigh) Fine. I'm in.", "me"): # float32 chunks at 24 kHz ... ``` `lure serve` starts an OpenAI-compatible speech server (`POST /v1/audio/speech`) that batches concurrent requests. ### qwen-tts (PyTorch) Lure uses the Qwen3-TTS 12Hz format, so the `qwen-tts` package loads it directly (without Turbo): ```python import soundfile as sf from qwen_tts import Qwen3TTSModel tts = Qwen3TTSModel.from_pretrained("Tesslate/Lure-TTS-0.6B", device_map="cuda:0", dtype="bfloat16") wavs, sr = tts.generate_voice_clone( text="I'm sorry. (sigh) I never meant for any of this to happen.", language="English", ref_audio="reference.wav", ref_text="Transcript of the reference clip.", non_streaming_mode=True, ) sf.write("out.wav", wavs[0], sr) ``` `qwen-tts` turns the direction (instruct) off for 0.6B models; use lure-tts if you want directions. ## Sound tags Write tags in round brackets, lowercase, at the spot where the sound should happen: `I can't believe it (laugh) you actually did it.` Square brackets like `[laugh]` are not supported. | Group | Tags | |---|---| | Laughter | `(laugh)` `(chuckle)` `(giggle)` `(nervous laugh)` `(wheezing laugh)` `(laughs while talking)` | | Breath | `(sigh)` `(frustrated sigh)` `(relieved sigh)` `(exhale)` `(inhale)` `(sharp inhale)` `(gasp)` `(happy gasp)` `(yawn)` | | Crying | `(voice breaking)` `(sob)` `(whimper)` `(sniff)` `(sniffle)` | | Throat and mouth | `(cough)` `(clears throat)` `(swallow)` `(gulp)` `(lip smack)` `(tsk)` `(snort)` `(grunt)` `(groan)` `(hum)` | | Spoken sounds | `(hmm)` `(ugh)` `(pfft)` `(scoff)` `(ow)` | | Timing | `(pause)` | - Laughs, sighs, gasps and sharp inhales are the most reliable. Rarer tags like `(ow)` or `(sob)` land less often. - One or two tags per sentence works best. - If a take misses a tag, regenerate with a new seed. ## Direction A direction is a short note to the actor about emotion, pace, pitch or breath. It is optional. Without one, Lure takes the delivery from the words and tags. - `Sudden, bright shock. Fast attack on the question, then a caught breath lifting pitch sharply upward.` - `Slow, stunned, hushed. Barely any pitch movement, like the brain is still buffering.` - `Tight, shivering disbelief. Thin voice, trembly pitch, the laugh escaping between clauses.` ## Recommended settings | Setting | Value | |---|---| | Language | `english` (always set it; `auto` uses a different prompt and hurts quality) | | Sampling | temperature 0.9, top-k 50, top-p 1.0, repetition penalty 1.05, same for the sub-talker | | Precision | bf16 | | Prompt layout | non-streaming (full text up front); lure-tts does this automatically | | Reference clip | 3 to 12 s, one speaker, clean, no music. The output inherits the clip's mic and room. | | Reference transcript | The exact words in the clip. A wrong transcript causes skipped or repeated words. | | Text per call | A sentence or short paragraph. For long text, split on sentences (lure-tts does this and streams each piece). | | Retry rule | If a take runs past twice its expected length or never stops, regenerate with a new seed. | ## Limitations - English only. Other languages have not been tested. - Directions shape emotion and pace well, but Lure is weaker than large instruction-tuned models at changing who is speaking (accent, age, gender) on request. - Sound tags are best effort; a take sometimes skips one. - Very long single calls can stop early or drift in voice. Split long text into sentences. - Do not use Lure to imitate a real person without their consent. Training data includes YODAS v3. ## License Apache 2.0 for everything: the weights, the [lure-tts](https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts) engine and the [lure-train](https://github.com/smirki/lure-train) training code.

Lure Turbo 0.6B

The Lure voice, about 1.7x faster end to end.
Research preview · English · 0.6B parameters · 24 kHz

[![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live%20demo-e8590c?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/smirki/lure-tts) [![Lure](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lure-7048e8?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/Tesslate/Lure-TTS-0.6B) [![Engine](https://img.shields.io/badge/Engine-1c7ed6?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts) [![Training code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Training%20code-2f9e44?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/smirki/lure-train)
> [!WARNING] > **Research preview.** Weights, behaviour and this card can change between releases. Pin a revision if you build on it. ## What Turbo changes Lure, like every Qwen3-TTS 12Hz model, makes each 80 ms audio frame in two stages. A large model picks the first of the frame's 16 codes, then a small code predictor fills in the other 15 one after another. Once the large model is fast, those 15 sequential passes take most of the time per frame. Lure Turbo replaces them with a head that predicts the 15 codes in 3 grouped passes (codes 1-3, 4-7 and 8-15). The size, voices, tags and directions are the same as Lure's. | Per frame, 24 GB GPU, 8 streams | Lure | Lure Turbo | |---|---|---| | Code predictor passes | 15 | **3** | | Code predictor time | 21.2 ms | **6.2 ms** | ## Speed Measured with the [lure-tts](https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts) engine, cuda backend, bf16. RTF is generation time divided by audio length, so lower is faster. | GPU | Model | Streams | RTF | |---|---|---|---| | H100 | Lure | 1 | 0.23 | | H100 | **Lure Turbo** | 1 | **0.14** | | H100 | Lure | 8 | 0.25 | | H100 | **Lure Turbo** | 8 | **0.15** | | 24 GB GPU | 1 stream | 8 streams, total | |---|---|---| | Lure | 2.3x real time | 17x real time | | **Lure Turbo** | **4.0x real time** | **30x real time** | ## Quality On every public benchmark we ran, Turbo scores the same as Lure (one take per line, official scripts): | | Seed-TTS WER ↓ | Seed-TTS SIM ↑ | LibriSpeech-PC WER ↓ | LibriSpeech-PC SIM ↑ | UTMOS ↑ | VDB SIM ↑ | CV3 emotion % ↑ | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Lure | 1.51 | 0.653 | 1.72 | 0.638 | 4.43 | 0.81 | 73.3 | | Lure Turbo | 1.59 | 0.654 | 1.84 | 0.641 | 4.38 | 0.81 | 73.3 | The full comparison with other models is on the [Lure card](https://huggingface.co/Tesslate/Lure-TTS-0.6B#benchmarks). ## Quick start The grouped head needs the [lure-tts](https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts) engine, which loads it automatically when `turbo.json` is in the model folder (mlx, cuda and C++ backends). Other Qwen3-TTS runtimes do not know the head. ```bash git clone https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts && cd lure-tts hf download Tesslate/Lure-TTS-Turbo --local-dir models/lure-turbo pip install ./backends/mlx ".[server]" # Mac; see the repo for NVIDIA and the C++ build ``` ```python from lure_tts import Lure tts = Lure.load("models/lure-turbo") voice = tts.make_voice("reference.wav", "Transcript of the reference clip.", name="me") for pcm in tts.stream("(gasp) No way. (laugh) You actually did it!", voice, instruct="Bright, giddy disbelief."): ... # float32 chunks at 24 kHz ``` Tags, directions and recommended settings are the same as Lure's; see the [Lure card](https://huggingface.co/Tesslate/Lure-TTS-0.6B#sound-tags). ## Limitations Same as Lure: English only, sound tags are best effort, and very long single calls should be split into sentences. Do not use it to imitate a real person without their consent. Training data includes YODAS v3. ## License Apache 2.0 for everything: the weights, the [lure-tts](https://github.com/smirki/lure-tts) engine and the [lure-train](https://github.com/smirki/lure-train) training code.

# 🦜 VieNeu-TTS v3 Turbo

[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Repository-blue)](https://github.com/pnnbao97/VieNeu-TTS)
[![Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hugging%20Face-Model-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/pnnbao-ump/VieNeu-TTS-v3-Turbo)
[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyPI-vieneu%203.7.1-blue?logo=pypi&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/vieneu/)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20Us-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/yJt8kzjzWZ)

## Overview

<video controls src="https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/68b923a86c86c127a1975eda/paPqSDpwFGrKtIZrqaEg4.mp4" width="100%"></video>

**VieNeu-TTS v3 Turbo** is the next generation of Vietnamese TTS — **48 kHz** high-fidelity speech, **23 built-in preset voices** across three regions (North / Central / South), **instant voice cloning**, **real-time streaming** with an **OpenAI-compatible API** (16 concurrent streams on one RTX 3060), inline **emotion cues**, and seamless **bilingual (En–Vi) code-switching**.

The reference implementation is the **`vieneu` Python SDK (v3.7.1)**. Its minimal install is **torch-free**: on CPU everything runs on **ONNX Runtime** (PyTorch is never imported), and on a CUDA machine it auto-switches to the PyTorch engine with **automatic batching** and a **continuous-batching stream scheduler** — same API, no code change.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **What's new in SDK v3.7:**
> - **GPU streaming with continuous batching** — `infer_stream` on CUDA runs on one CUDA graph shared by every caller: first audio in **~115 ms**, **16 concurrent streams under 200 ms** on a single RTX 3060 (32 max).
> - **OpenAI-compatible streaming API + Docker** — `POST /v1/audio/speech` (`pcm`/`wav`, chunked or SSE) works with the OpenAI SDK, Pipecat, LiveKit; `docker compose --profile api-gpu` / `api-cpu`. Numbers, sizing and CPU-only notes: [docs/streaming.md](https://github.com/pnnbao97/VieNeu-TTS/blob/main/docs/streaming.md).
> - **23 preset voices** covering North / Central / South, both genders and several reading characters (default: `Minh Quân`).
> - **LoRA fine-tuning** of v3 Turbo on one consumer GPU.
> - Since 3.3: torch-free voice cloning on CPU, optional **int8** CPU backbone (`Vieneu(precision="int8")`, ~2× faster; fp32 is the default), sliding-window repetition penalty.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Credits

The **VieNeu-TTS v3 Turbo architecture is an original design by the author, Phạm Nguyễn Ngọc Bảo**, and is **trained from scratch** on ~10,000 hours of English–Vietnamese speech — it is **not** a fine-tune, distillation, or adaptation of any existing TTS model.

- **Model architecture & training:** designed and trained from scratch by **Phạm Nguyễn Ngọc Bảo** — https://github.com/pnnbao97
- **Audio codec:** [MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano) (OpenMOSS-Team) — 48 kHz neural audio codec.
- **Phonemizer:** [sea-g2p](https://github.com/pnnbao97/sea-g2p) — fast Vietnamese/English grapheme-to-phoneme, also by the author.

Tác giả: **Phạm Nguyễn Ngọc Bảo**

cd VieNeu-TTS
```

  ```

```bash

```

The UI opens at `http://127.0.0.1:7860` with a **Default voice** tab, a **Voice Cloning** tab, and a **Conversation** tab (batched multi-speaker podcasts).

## 📦 Using the Python SDK (`vieneu`)

**CPU (default)** — torch-free, runs v3 Turbo via ONNX Runtime. Most users want this:

```bash
pip install vieneu
```

**GPU (CUDA)** — only if you have an NVIDIA GPU; install a CUDA build of PyTorch yourself first:

```bash
pip install torch==2.8.0 torchaudio==2.8.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
pip install "transformers==4.57.6"   # Qwen3 backbone + MOSS codec (pinned — most stable)
pip install vieneu
```

> ℹ️ **When is GPU actually worth it?** Two cases: **bulk / long-form synthesis** (many chunks share one batched forward) and **serving many listeners** (the stream scheduler batches every `infer_stream` call — 16 concurrent real-time streams on an RTX 3060). For a **single short, interactive call** the torch-free **CPU/ONNX** path is fast enough (first audio ~140 ms with int8, ~300 ms with fp32) and needs no GPU.

### Full features guide

```python
from vieneu import Vieneu
from time import time

# Default = v3 Turbo (48 kHz). CPU → ONNX (torch-free, fp32); GPU → PyTorch (auto-detected).
tts = Vieneu()                    # fp32 backbone (default, max fidelity)
# tts = Vieneu(precision="int8")  # CPU only: ~2x faster, needs a CPU with VNNI

text = """[cười] Trời ơi, cái giọng nó tự nhiên mà nó mượt mà dã man, nghe không khác gì người thật luôn. Giờ thì tha hồ mà quẩy content với cả kho giọng nói đa dạng, đủ mọi sắc thái biểu cảm. Mọi người bật loa lên rồi cùng trải nghiệm thử với mình nhé!"""

# 1. Default voice (Minh Quân) — 48 kHz, no reference needed
start = time()
audio = tts.infer(text)
tts.save(audio, "output.wav")
print(f"Time taken: {time() - start:.2f} seconds")

# 2. Built-in voices by name
for label, voice_id in tts.list_preset_voices():
    print(label, voice_id)
audio = tts.infer("Mình là Xuân Vĩnh nè!", voice="Xuân Vĩnh")
tts.save(audio, "output_xuan_vinh.wav")

# 3. Emotion / non-verbal cues — EXPERIMENTAL: [cười] [thở dài] [hắng giọng]
audio = tts.infer("Nghe hay quá đi [cười]. Để mình nói tiếp [hắng giọng].", voice="Phạm Tuyên")

# 4. Instant voice cloning from a 3–8s reference clip (works on the torch-free CPU install too)
audio = tts.infer("Đây là giọng được nhân bản tức thì.", ref_audio="my_voice.wav", denoise=True)
```

> [!TIP]
> A **temperature around 0.8** gives the most stable result for v3 Turbo. Higher values add expressiveness but can be less stable.

### 🔊 Real-time streaming

v3 Turbo streams frame by frame on both backends. **GPU**: first audio in **~115 ms**, and every `infer_stream` call shares one CUDA graph (continuous batching) — **16 concurrent streams stay real-time** on a single RTX 3060 (RTF ≈ 0.5–0.6, 32 streams max). **CPU** (ONNX): first audio ~140 ms (int8) / ~300 ms (fp32), RTF < 1, one stream (two with int8).

```python
vieneu = Vieneu()   # GPU → PyTorch + stream scheduler; no GPU → ONNX/CPU
for chunk in vieneu.infer_stream("Xin chào! Đây là chế độ streaming của VieNeu, phát tới đâu nghe tới đó.", voice="Mai Anh"):
    play(chunk)   # np.float32 @ 48 kHz, play/write as it arrives
```

**OpenAI-compatible API** — `POST /v1/audio/speech` (`pcm`/`wav`, chunked body or SSE), drop-in for the OpenAI SDK, Pipecat, LiveKit:

```bash
uv run python -m apps.openai_speech                                  # → http://localhost:8000
# (or: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile api-gpu up)
```

```python
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="x")
with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(
    model="vieneu-v3-turbo", voice="Mai Anh", response_format="pcm",
    input="Xin chào! Đây là chế độ streaming của VieNeu, phát tới đâu nghe tới đó.",
) as r:
    for chunk in r.iter_bytes(4096):   # s16le 48 kHz mono, as it is generated
        play(chunk)
```

All measurements (TTFA / RTF / streams vs `max_streams` on an RTX 3060), estimates for smaller GPUs and the CPU-only numbers: [docs/streaming.md](https://github.com/pnnbao97/VieNeu-TTS/blob/main/docs/streaming.md).

### ⚡ Batched generation (GPU)

`infer_batch()` runs many texts in **one batched forward** — same API on every backend (on CPU it still works, just sequentially). The batch caps at `max_batch_size` (default 32); pass `batch_size=1` to disable. A single long `infer()` also auto-batches its own chunks.

```python
audios = vieneu.infer_batch(texts, voice="Mai Anh")   # or infer_batch(..., batch_size=64)
```

### 🦜 Voice cloning & saved voices

```python
# Clone from a 3–8s clip; the reference is auto-denoised and trimmed to ≤ 8s
audio = vieneu.infer("Chào bạn, đây là giọng của tôi.", ref_audio="voice.wav", denoise=True)

# Enroll once, then reuse by name like a built-in voice
vieneu.add_voice("Giọng của tôi", "voice.wav")
audio = vieneu.infer("Câu này dùng giọng đã lưu.", voice="Giọng của tôi")

# Just clean up a clip (no synthesis)
wav, sr = vieneu.denoise("noisy.wav", out_path="clean.wav")
```

> `denoise`, `add_voice` and cloning work on **every** backend, including the torch-free CPU/ONNX install.

### ⚠️ Reading style is deprecated

`style` is **still accepted** by `infer`, `infer_stream`, `infer_batch` and `add_voice` so existing code keeps running, but it is **ignored** on v3 Turbo: the reading style is already baked into the reference itself (the speaker embedding + reference codes of the preset voice or of your cloned clip). Pick the reading character through the **voice** instead.

# PolyPlex-11B-CJKE **A full-duplex spoken dialogue model for Chinese, Japanese, Korean and English**

Quickstart · The tokenizer · The processor · Lineage · License · Citation

> [!NOTE] > **Preview release: tokenizer and processor only.** This repository currently ships the PolyPlex text tokenizer and the > input processor. The model weights will be added to this repository when training is finished. Everything below runs > on upstream `transformers` today; no fork is needed. ## ✨ Highlights - **A vocabulary sized by speech, not by text.** Every token of a full-duplex model fills one 80 ms frame. The vocabulary was grown language by language until words stop being cut by the next word on real conversational speech, measured on Whisper word timings of YouTube speech in 110 languages. - **223,973 tokens, smaller than Gemma 3.** Helium (Moshi's vocabulary) is kept with its ids, Qwen3's tokens are merged in, and whole words and subwords are added only where speech needs them. Written-only Qwen3 words that speech never uses are dropped. - **No byte fragments in speech.** Every standard character of every language is a token, so speech never falls back to bytes, which cannot be aligned to sound. - **Drop-in for 🤗 Transformers.** `AutoTokenizer` and `AutoProcessor` load it with stock `transformers`; the processor builds the frame-aligned text, user-audio and assistant-audio streams, including the PersonaPlex persona prompt. ## 🚀 Quickstart ```bash pip install "transformers>=5.14" torch ``` ### Tokenizer ```python from transformers import AutoTokenizer tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("RetentionLabs/PolyPlex-11B-CJKE") tokenizer.tokenize("안녕하세요, 반갑습니다.") # ['▁안녕하세요', ',', '▁반갑습니다', '.'] tokenizer.tokenize("Hello there!") # ['▁Hello', '▁there', '!'] tokenizer.tokenize("你好，很高兴认识你") # ['▁', '你好', '，', '很高兴', '认识', '你'] tokenizer.tokenize("こんにちは、元気ですか") # ['▁', 'こんにちは', '、', '元', '気', 'ですか'] tokenizer.pad_token_id, tokenizer.unk_token_id # (3, 0): PAD and EPAD of the duplex text stream ``` ### Processor The processor loads the [Mimi](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/mimi) codec and turns text and audio into the three frame-aligned streams the model reads. ```python import numpy as np from transformers import AutoProcessor processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("RetentionLabs/PolyPlex-11B-CJKE", trust_remote_code=True) speech = np.zeros(24_000 * 2, dtype=np.float32) # 2 s of user speech at 24 kHz inputs = processor(text="안녕하세요", audio=speech) # input_ids (1, 25) text padded with PAD to one token per frame # user_audio_codes (1, 8, 25) Mimi codes of the user's speech # assistant_audio_codes (1, 8, 25) encoded silence, since no assistant audio was given prompt = processor(text_prompt="You are a friendly assistant who speaks Korean.") # persona prefix waveform = processor.decode_audio(inputs["user_audio_codes"]) # (1, 1, 48000) ``` ## 🔤 The tokenizer ### Why a duplex model needs its own vocabulary A text LLM can cut a rare word into many pieces: the sequence only gets longer. A full-duplex speech model writes its text stream in step with audio, **one token per 80 ms frame** (Moshi, PersonaPlex). A word must fit in the frames between its own onset and the next word's onset. When it does not, the next word overwrites its tail and the word is **cut** (Moshi, Section 3.4.4, Eq. 5). Byte fragments are worse still: a fragment of a UTF-8 character matches no sound at all. Qwen3's byte-level BPE, for example, cuts 14.5% of the tokens of spoken Korean into byte fragments, 96% of them at a word's first character. So the PolyPlex vocabulary is designed around one measurable quantity. > **Word cut rate**: the share of words whose tokens do not all survive in the text stream when the words are placed at > their real onsets, one token per frame, the way the model is trained. ### Construction | Step | What | Size | |---|---|---| | **1. Base** | Helium (Moshi's SentencePiece vocabulary) keeps every token and id. Qwen3's tokens are added with the leading space written as `▁` (`Ġword` → `▁word`); a string both have is one token, Helium's. Every string is NFC. | 32,000 + Qwen3 | | **2. Tier 1: characters** | Every standard character of each language (CLDR 48.2.3 exemplars, plus the full Unicode block for Indic, Southeast Asian and Georgian scripts), each also as a word-start form `▁c` for letters and digits. Unconditional. | 13,457 new | | **3. Tier 2: whole words** | Frequent spoken word forms that take two or more tokens, ordered by frames saved (count × (tokens − 1)), added 250 at a time while the cut rate falls. | 20,168 | | **4. Tier 3: subwords** | Subwords from a Unigram model trained on each language's multi-token spoken words, added 1,000 at a time while the cut rate falls, plus non-standard characters of the language's own scripts seen three or more times. | 64,228 | | **5. Scores** | Unigram scores by EM over the spoken text of every language, with the vocabulary fixed. | | | **6. Pruning** | Qwen3 multi-character tokens the spoken EM never uses are dropped (written Chinese and English words, symbol runs), as are unused word-start forms of single Han and kana characters. Code pieces, emoji and single characters are kept for tool use. | −30,685 | For each language, both orders are run (subwords first, then whole words; and whole words first, then subwords), and the order that reaches the target with fewer tokens is kept. A subword shortens every word that holds it, so subwords win for scripts where words take many tokens (Greek: 5,016 subwords instead of 21,016 tokens; Hindi: 6,000 instead of 19,500); whole words win where a few hundred to a few thousand forms suffice (Korean: 3,750 words). ### Measuring the cut rate - **Speech.** User-subtitled YouTube videos of [YODAS2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/espnet/yodas2) in every language that has them, Korean included. Neighbouring subtitle segments are joined into pieces of at most 25 s. - **Word timings.** Whisper large-v3, with the transcript forced (teacher forcing) and DTW over the alignment heads' cross-attention. The timings are released as [RetentionLabs/polyplex-word-timings](https://huggingface.co/datasets/RetentionLabs/polyplex-word-timings). - **Filtering.** Pieces whose alignment loss exceeds 1.61 (the 95th percentile on KsponSpeech) are subtitles that do not match the speech. Pieces where over 10% of neighbouring onsets are under 20 ms apart were not aligned. A word whose span or gap is under 30 ms per character is an alignment error: it keeps its frames but counts neither as cut nor in the total. - **Approximation.** Languages left with fewer than 2,000 timed words, and scripts without spaces, place words by their share of characters in the utterance duration (FLEURS recordings, or the script's characters per second). - **Targets.** 1%, or the lowest reachable rate (every word one token) plus 0.2 points when that is higher. The main languages, English, Korean, Japanese and Chinese, go on to the lowest rate plus 0.2 points even below 1%. ### Result Final cut rates are measured with the final tokenizer on the evaluation part of each language, held out from selection. | Language | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Word cut rate | Target | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | English | 10 | 0 | 0 | 0.18% | 0.28% | | Korean | 2,432 | 3,750 | 48 | 0.23% | 0.23% | | Japanese | 8,817 | 0 | 3 | 0.00% | 0.20% | | Chinese (Simplified) | 6,850 | 0 | 3 | 0.00% | 0.20% | | Chinese (Traditional) | 6,801 | 0 | 98 | 0.03% | 0.20% | | Cantonese | 6,801 | 0 | 0 | 0.01% | 1.00% | Across all 110 measured languages the median cut rate is 0.25%, and 109 are below their target. Punjabi stays at 1.97%: it has no subtitles in OpenSubtitles and five YODAS2 shards, so its candidate text is 2,198 lines. It is left above the target rather than filled with written text. | Vocabulary | Size | |---|---:| | Helium (Moshi, PersonaPlex) | 32,000 | | Llama 3 | 128,256 | | Qwen3 | 151,669 | | **PolyPlex** | **223,973** | | Gemma 3 | 262,144 | ### Layout and behaviour | Item | Value | |---|---| | Model | SentencePiece-style Unigram with byte fallback (`tokenizers`) | | Normalization | NFC, then spaces to `▁` with one `▁` in front of the text | | Word starts | Marked by `▁` on the first token of every word. `EPAD` marks the end of a pause and is skipped when the previous word still occupies its frame (Moshi), so it cannot mark word starts. | | Digits | One token per digit; no multi-digit tokens exist | | Ids 0 – 31,999 | Helium, unchanged: `` = 0 (`EPAD` in the duplex stream), `` = 1, `` = 2, `` = 3 (`PAD`), bytes 4 – 259 | | Ids 32,000 – 32,005 | Control tokens `` `` `` `` `` `` | | Ids 32,006 – 223,972 | The rest of the base block, then one block per script, each ordered by score | | LM head | 224,000 rows (padded to a multiple of 128). The opening frame id is 224,000 and exists only as an input row. | Control and special tokens never come out of text: their Unigram score lies far below every text piece, so a literal `` in text is cut as `▁<` `think` `>`. The id range of each script block is stored as `blocks` in `tokenizer_config.json`. A script-group output head (the base block plus one script's block) can be cut from it:

# OmniVoice-BG

A Bulgarian text-to-speech model, fine-tuned from
[**k2-fsa/OmniVoice**](https://huggingface.co/k2-fsa/OmniVoice). It produces
**natural, native-sounding Bulgarian** speech, removing the foreign accent that stock
OmniVoice has on Bulgarian — and, in this revision, it renders **imperative
(final-stress) verb forms** correctly on voices it has never heard.

> **This revision (ft9b) replaces the narration-only release of June 2026.** The older
> weights are still available on the `v1-narration-2026-06` branch
> (`revision="v1-narration-2026-06"`) if you depend on them. The change is additive in
> intent — it is the same narration model, fine-tuned further on imperative stress —
> but general narration quality was not re-benchmarked, so if narration is all you need
> and you have validated the old weights, there is no reason to move.

> These are the fine-tuned **weights only**. The full OmniVoice-BG system has two more
> serving-side pillars — a lexical **stress front-end** and **deterministic fixed-voice
> cloning** — which are not baked into the weights.

## What this revision fixes, and what it does not

Bulgarian marks grammatical role with stress position, and the same spelling takes
different stress depending on that role: **хо́ди** "(s)he walks" against **ходи́** "walk!".
Getting the imperative right had defeated four previous fine-tunes (ft4–ft8): stress
transferred only to voices present in training, because from a handful of clips per
(verb, voice) the model memorised timbre rather than abstracting a text→stress rule.

**Fixed.** For **ходи**, this checkpoint renders *both* roles correctly on **held-out
reference voices** — ходи́ as an imperative and хо́ди as a 3rd-person present. That it
gets both right is the point: it learned where the mark goes, not a flipped default.

**Not fixed.** For **прави**, the imperative is still wrong on male and mid-pitch
voices (correct on female). The cause is measured, not guessed: imperative exposure in
the training mix is near-identical between the two verbs (ходи 504 rows, прави 488),
but *stem* exposure differs 12-fold — хо́ди 55 against пра́ви 660, because пра́ви "does"
saturates ordinary narration. So ходи́ wins its stress-role contest 9.2:1 while прави́
is out-voted 0.7:1. A follow-up run that rebalanced прави to 3.4:1 exists but is not
released, because it has not been fully validated by ear.

Practical consequence: **do not rely on this model for imperative-heavy copy without
listening.** Non-resistant imperatives (обади́, купи́, наслади́, вдигни́) were already
reliable and remain so.

## Model details

- **Architecture:** `OmniVoice` — a diffusion/mask-prediction language model predicting
  Higgs Audio V2 codec tokens (8 codebooks @ 24 kHz). Backbone `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`.
- **Base model:** [`k2-fsa/OmniVoice`](https://huggingface.co/k2-fsa/OmniVoice) (Apache-2.0)
- **Lineage:** stock OmniVoice → Bulgarian narration (audiobooks) → **ft9b**, this revision
- **Sample rate:** 24 kHz mono · **Size:** ~2.45 GB (`model.safetensors`)

### Training

Fine-tuned for 3,000 steps (38 min on one 16 GB GPU) from the Bulgarian narration
checkpoint. Full config in [`train_config.json`](./train_config.json), data mix in
[`data_config.json`](./data_config.json).

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| init from | Bulgarian narration checkpoint (step 6500) |
| steps | 3000 |
| learning rate | 5e-6, cosine, 5% warmup |
| batch | `batch_tokens=1024`, `grad_accum=8`, `max_batch_size=8` |
| precision | bf16 mixed · attention SDPA |
| weight decay | 0.01 · seed 42 |

### Data mix

Five token streams — two of ordinary narration, three of imperatives. Narration stays
dominant by volume; the imperative streams carry high `repeat` weights because they are
tiny. All text is **stress-marked** (vowel + U+0301).

| Stream | Source | Size | `repeat` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Narration, main | [`beleata74/bulgarian-audiobooks-tts-400h`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/beleata74/bulgarian-audiobooks-tts-400h) — single female narrator, 24 kHz, MIT | 193,768 clips ≈ 448 h | 1× plain + 4× sparse-reference twin |
| Narration, base | [`raditotev/bg-audiobooks-tts`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/raditotev/bg-audiobooks-tts) — single narrator, CC0 | 10,095 clips ≈ 14.4 h | 1× plain + 4× sparse-reference twin |
| Imperatives, synthetic | Teacher distillation from [`beleata74/BgTTS-38M-V2`](https://huggingface.co/beleata74/BgTTS-38M-V2), labelled by a Kaldi forced aligner; 164 verbs × 22 frames, 4 reference voices | 6,648 clips | 8× |
| Imperatives, human | Own recordings, one voice — the two verbs the teacher cannot say (прави́ / ходи́) | 30 clips | 12× |
| Imperatives, **volunteer** | 11 real speakers, 483 accepted takes, head speakers capped and tail voices sox-perturbed into pseudo-speakers | 868 rows | 4× |

Dev set: the sparse-reference dev splits of the two narration corpora.

Two notes on why the mix looks like this. The **sparse-reference twins** are the same
audio re-tokenised in the short-prompt style the serving layer uses, weighted 4× so the
model is good at the condition it actually runs in. And **прави/ходи are deliberately
absent from the synthetic set**: the BgTTS teacher renders them with stem stress, so
including them would have taught the error — they come from the human and volunteer
streams instead.

The volunteer stream is the component that made the difference. Earlier fine-tunes
(ft4–ft8) had the synthetic and human sets but not many real timbres per verb, and
imperative stress stayed voice-specific. The measured lesson was that the gain tracks
**distinct-voice exposure per verb**, not clip count, which is why this revision exempts
the resistant verbs from the head-speaker cap (прави 12 → 72 rows / 4 voices, ходи
20 → 81 rows / 5 voices).

The narration also enters a second time, through the initialisation: step 6500 of the
413 h Bulgarian narration run, trained on the same two corpora.

### Why the released checkpoint is not the lowest-loss one

Validation loss over the run is flat and noisy — 3.738 to 3.812 across all twelve eval
points, best at step 1250, with the released step-3000 checkpoint at 3.786. **Eval loss
does not track stress correctness at this scale.** The checkpoint was selected by
blind listening on held-out reference voices, with each verb rendered in *both*
grammatical roles so that a gain in the imperative could not hide a regression in the
3rd-person present. TensorBoard logs are in [`tensorboard/`](./tensorboard).

## Usage

```bash
pip install omnivoice

omnivoice-infer \
    --model preslaff/omnivoice-bg \
    --text "Ходи́ на разходка всяка сутрин." \
    --ref_audio narrator.wav \
    --output out.wav
```

```python
from omnivoice import OmniVoice

model = OmniVoice.from_pretrained("preslaff/omnivoice-bg", train=False)
wav = model.generate(
    text="Ходи́ на разходка всяка сутрин.",   # stress marked with U+0301
    ref_audio="narrator.wav",                # fixed reference for consistent cloning
)
```

> **Mark the stress.** This model is trained on text carrying combining acute accents
> (vowel + U+0301) and will not infer Bulgarian lexical stress from bare text. Pass
> marked text, use a fixed reference clip, and seed decoding for reproducibility — the
> OmniVoice-BG server does all three automatically.

## Related

- Bulgarian ASR from the same project:
  [bulgarian-asr-zipformer](https://huggingface.co/preslaff/bulgarian-asr-zipformer)
  (3.93% WER) and its
  [streaming twin](https://huggingface.co/preslaff/bulgarian-asr-zipformer-streaming)
- Written benchmark and method notes: [asr.cdsv.dev](https://asr.cdsv.dev)

## License & attribution

Apache-2.0, a derivative of **OmniVoice** by k2-fsa (Apache-2.0); base model and
architecture © Xiaomi Corp. Narration data:
[`raditotev/bg-audiobooks-tts`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/raditotev/bg-audiobooks-tts)
(CC0) and
[`beleata74/bulgarian-audiobooks-tts-400h`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/beleata74/bulgarian-audiobooks-tts-400h)
(MIT). The synthetic imperative set was distilled from
[`beleata74/BgTTS-38M-V2`](https://huggingface.co/beleata74/BgTTS-38M-V2) (Apache-2.0).

The volunteer imperative recordings that made this revision possible are **not
published** — the speakers consented to their voices being used for training, not to
redistribution of the audio, and no contact details were ever collected. Thank you to
the 11 people who recorded them.

gpt-sovits - gpt-sovits-v2proplus - chinese - character-voice - galgame - anime --- # TangYuGe GPT-SoVITS v2ProPlus 针对视觉小说 *Sparkling Memories (夏日花火)* 中角色 *Tang Yuge (唐语歌)* 的声音微调的 [GPT-SoVITS](https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS) **v2ProPlus** 权重。仅支持中文（普通话），输出为 32 kHz 单声道。 本仓库包含完整配套内容：微调后的 GPT 和 SoVITS 权重、19 个场景配置及其参考音频和提示文本、推理 / HTTP 桥接脚本，以及运行或继续训练所需的全部辅助模型和基础模型（可选择下载）。当前版本：**GPT `G-F2+DPO` 第 10 轮 + SoVITS 第 4 轮**（`weights/tangyuge_v2pp_dpo-e10.ckpt`、`weights/tangyuge_v2pp_e4_s564.pth`）。 | | | | --- | --- | | 任务 | 语音合成、少样本声音克隆（角色声音） | | 语言 | 仅限中文普通话 | | 输出 | 32 kHz，单声道，WAV | | 权重 | GPT 155 MB + SoVITS 173 MB（fp16） | | 验证环境 | GPT-SoVITS commit `ea2d2a8`、Python 3.10、PyTorch 2.4.0 + CUDA 12.4、RTX 4060 Laptop（8 GB） | | 实时率 | 在上述已验证 GPU 上约为 0.4–0.5（fp16，预热后） | | 许可证 | Apache-2.0（见[许可与权利](#licensing-and-rights)） | ## 模型详情 ### 模型描述 - **维护者：** shiqianyan - **模型类型：** 两阶段自回归 TTS。由 GPT（文本 → 语义 token）和 SoVITS（语义 token + 参考音频 → 波形）组成，两者均从官方 v2ProPlus 基础模型进行全量微调（非 LoRA）。 - **语言：** 中文普通话 - **微调基础模型：** [`lj1995/GPT-SoVITS`](https://huggingface.co/lj1995/GPT-SoVITS)（`s1v3.ckpt`、`v2Pro/s2Gv2ProPlus.pth`、`v2Pro/s2Dv2ProPlus.pth`） - **来源：** 训练代码采用官方 GPT-SoVITS（commit `ea2d2a8`）；仅新增学习率调度启动器及官方 DPO 选项的开关（见[训练流程](#training-procedure)）。 ### 版本历史 `main` 始终保存当前版本。较早的 GPT 检查点以标签形式保留。 | 标签 / 引用 | GPT 检查点 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `main`（标签 `v2pp-dpo-e10-20261023`） | `weights/tangyuge_v2pp_dpo-e10.ckpt` | **当前版本。** 真实录音 + 合成教师数据，学习率余弦退火，官方 DPO | | `v2pp-d2-20261022` | `weights/tangyuge_v2pp_d2-e6.ckpt` | 蒸馏轮次：561 条真实录音 + 561 条合成音频，比例为 1:1（该标签的 `weights/` 中仍有 e14 文件；请使用 d2 文件） | | `v2pp-e14-20261020` | `weights/tangyuge_v2pp-e14.ckpt` | 首个 v2ProPlus 版本：仅使用 561 条真实录音训练 | 三个版本的 SoVITS 权重（`tangyuge_v2pp_e4_s564.pth`）完全相同。 ```bash hf download shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus --revision v2pp-d2-20261022 --local-dir TangYuGe-d2 ``` 较早的 v2Pro（非 Plus）微调版本位于 [shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2Pro](https://huggingface.co/shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2Pro)。v2ProPlus 系列的底噪和背景噪声明显更低（见 `manifests/training_report.md`），建议使用该系列。 ## 用途 ### 直接用途 以该角色的声音生成中文对白，用于同人作品、游戏模组、角色聊天机器人以及个人学习或研究。请选择与台词语气相符的场景配置（见[场景配置](#scene-profiles)）；参考音频及其提示文本在很大程度上决定情感和节奏。 ### 不适用的用途 非中文文本；中英混合文本（未经测试）；任何需要原配音演员精确表演的用途；冒充真实人物；误导性或违法用途。请将生成音频标注为 AI 合成。 ## 偏差、风险与局限 - **短句**可能提前结束（例如，四个音节的台词只说出前半部分）。这是 GPT-SoVITS 自回归解码的已知特性；下文较保守的默认采样参数可以减少此类情况，但无法完全避免。 - **电音 / “含混”伪影。** 部分输出，尤其是使用严肃场景参考音频（`serious_script41_L0682`，即 `main_hybrid_mid` 的默认参考音频）时，存在轻微电子失真或“嘴里含着东西”的听感。这些伪影存在于随仓库发布的 SoVITS 第 4 轮权重中，后续所有实验均**未能**修复。自动指标（DNSMOS、ASR 错误率）无法检测到这些问题，因此本版本不声称有所改善。 - **非语音声音**（笑声、吸气、叹气）在 GPT-SoVITS 中没有专用 token（音素词表已满）。只有当文本包含嘻嘻 / 哈哈 / 唉等感叹词时才会出现，质量也低于自然笑声。在我们的测试中，约四分之三的预期事件类型得以呈现（事件召回率为 0.77，见[评测](#evaluation)）。 - 参考音频与**提示文本必须配对**。错误的提示文本会明显降低发音和节奏质量。 - 声音与音色受限于约 43 分钟的源录音；强烈情感（喊叫、哭泣）的表现较弱。 - 在部分 Intel 混合架构 CPU 上（已在 i7-13650HX 上复现），PyTorch 的 oneDNN 多线程 `Conv1d` 会返回错误结果。GPU 推理不受影响；使用 CPU 时，请设置 `torch.backends.mkldnn.enabled = False` 或以单线程运行。 - 部分 GPT 训练数据是由商业 TTS 服务模仿同一角色生成的合成语音。这些数据不在此处重新分发，也可能将该服务自身的发音错误传递给模型。 ### 建议 保留默认采样参数，选择与文本最接近的场景配置，发布前试听输出，并且不要用它模仿真实人物。 ## 快速上手 ### 1. 准备 GPT-SoVITS ```bash git clone https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS.git cd GPT-SoVITS && git checkout ea2d2a8 # 按照上游文档安装其 Python 依赖 ``` ### 2. 下载本仓库 将其放在 `GPT-SoVITS/` 旁边： ```bash cd .. && hf download shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus --local-dir TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus ``` 如果你已在使用 GPT-SoVITS v2ProPlus，并已具备其辅助模型（BERT、HuBERT、SV、G2PW、fast_langdetect），则只需下载权重、场景配置、参考音频和脚本；可以跳过体积较大的覆盖目录： ```bash hf download shiqianyan/TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus --exclude "GPT-SoVITS-overlay/*" --local-dir TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus ``` ### 3. 安装辅助模型（已有则可跳过） ```bash python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus/scripts/install_pretrained.py --gptsovits-root GPT-SoVITS ``` 该脚本会校验哈希，并将 `GPT-SoVITS-overlay/` 复制到 GPT-SoVITS 目录树中（跳过已有且内容相同的文件）。覆盖目录包含两组内容： | 类别 | 文件 | 用途 | | --- | --- | --- | | 辅助模型 | `chinese-roberta-wwm-ext-large`（BERT）、`chinese-hubert-base`、`sv/`（说话人验证）、`text/G2PWModel`、`fast_langdetect` | **推理** | | 官方 v2ProPlus 基础模型 | `v2Pro/s2Gv2ProPlus.pth`、`v2Pro/s2Dv2ProPlus.pth`、`s1v3.ckpt` | 仅用于继续训练 | 微调权重是完整的推理模型。GPT-SoVITS 保存时会移除后验编码器（`enc_q`）和判别器，因此从这些权重继续训练时，需要使用基础模型恢复这些部分。 ### 4. 合成语音 使用 GPT-SoVITS 的 Python 环境： ```bash # 默认配置（严肃语气 / 长句） python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus/scripts/run_tangyuge_infer.py --text "这里填写要合成的中文文本。" --output output.wav # 其他场景：切换配置 python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus/scripts/run_tangyuge_infer.py \ --voice-profile TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus/profiles/morning.yaml \ --text "早上好呀，今天也要元气满满哦。" --output morning.wav ``` 如果两个目录不在同一父目录下，请添加 `--gptsovits-root `；添加 `--seed N` 可复现结果。 ### 5. HTTP 服务（可选） ```bash python TangYuGe-GPT-SoVITS-v2ProPlus/scripts/start_tangyuge_bridge.py ``` 该服务在 `127.0.0.1:9881` 提供 `/tts` 接口（GPT-SoVITS 的 `api_v2` 后端运行在 `9880`）。桥接服务会根据文本选择场景，你也可以指定场景： ```python import requests r = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:9881/tts", json={"text": "早上好呀，今天也要元气满满哦。", "profile": "morning"}, # "profile" 为可选字段 timeout=120, ) open("output.wav", "wb").write(r.content) ``` 请求字段：`text`（必填）、`profile` / `scene` / `reference`（选择场景）、`top_k`、`top_p`、`temperature`，以及常用的 `api_v2` 字段。辅助接口：`GET /health`、`GET /profiles`、`GET /references`。 如果直接调用原生 GPT-SoVITS `api_v2` 后端，权重由服务端固定，但**每个请求仍必须携带场景参考音频及其提示文本**（取自 `manifests/references.yaml`）： ```json { "text": "早上好呀，今天也要元气满满哦。", "text_lang": "zh", "ref_audio_path": "/references/morning_script43_L0993.wav", "prompt_text": "曦铭？这么早就来学校了呀。", "prompt_lang": "zh", "top_k": 5, "top_p": 0.8, "temperature": 0.7, "text_split_method": "cut5", "batch_size": 1, "media_type": "wav", "streaming_mode": false } ``` ### 6. GPT-SoVITS WebUI 安装辅助模型后，选择 GPT 权重 `weights/tangyuge_v2pp_dpo-e10.ckpt`、SoVITS 权重 `weights/tangyuge_v2pp_e4_s564.pth`、`references/` 中的任一音频及其在 `manifests/references.yaml` 中对应的 `prompt_text`，并使用下列采样参数。 ### 默认参数 | 参数 | 值 | | --- | --- | | `top_k` / `top_p` / `temperature` | `5` / `0.8` / `0.7`（较保守；相比上游默认值更少出现吞音节） | | 文本切分 | `cut5` | | 精度 | fp16（fp32 未显示出可测量的差异） | | 重复惩罚 | 上游默认值（1.35）；1.0 和 1.15 均未带来改善 | ### 配置格式 每个配置通过相对路径绑定权重、配置文件、参考音频和提示文本，因此仓库可移动到任意位置： ```yaml # 节选 name: tangyuge_v2pp_final_main version: v2ProPlus tts_config: ../configs/tts_infer_pack.yaml weights: gpt: ../weights/tangyuge_v2pp_dpo-e10.ckpt sovits: ../weights/tangyuge_v2pp_e4_s564.pth prompt: reference_id: serious_script41_L0682 ref_audio_path: ../references/serious_script41_L0682.wav prompt_text: 气也撒了，如果你还不收敛，给在场辛苦的工作人员增添麻烦，丢人现眼的，也只有你自己了。 prompt_lang: zh defaults: {text_lang: zh, text_split_method: cut5, media_type: wav, batch_size: 1, top_k: 5, top_p: 0.8, temperature: 0.7} ``` ### 场景配置 GPT-SoVITS 的语气和节奏主要取决于参考音频，因此仓库提供了 19 个场景参考（每个均为游戏原始台词音频及其转写文本），以 `profiles/*.yaml` 形式打包： | 配置 | 适用场景 | | --- | --- | | `main_hybrid_mid`（默认） | 严肃说明、长句、平稳情绪 | | `morning` | 问候、简短闲聊 | | `neutral_polite` | 平实陈述、礼貌回复 | | `soft_daily` | 温柔、轻松的日常交谈 | | `question_clear` / `question_firm` | 关切询问 / 质问 | | `lively_daily` / `casual_invite` | 轻快短句 / 邀请朋友 | | `narration_calm` | 旁白 | | `apology` | 道歉、礼貌退让 | | `bright_fireworks` / `high_brightness_exclaim` / `exclaim` | 明快期待 / 开心短句 / 惊讶感叹 | | `intimate_reassure` / `romantic_soft` | 亲密安慰 / 羞涩的浪漫台词 | | `command_gentle` | 提醒、劝阻 | | `food_daily` / `cafeteria_ordering` | 美食话题 / 点餐 | | `low_energy_discussion` | 克制的说明、平静讨论 | 更换参考音频时，也要同时更换其提示文本。 ### 样例 | 文件 | 文本 | | --- | --- | | [`samples/sample_morning.wav`](samples/sample_morning.wav) | 早上好呀，今天也要元气满满哦。 | | [`samples/sample_long_statement.wav`](samples/sample_long_statement.wav) | 这个计划我已经反复确认过了，如果大家都愿意配合，烟火大会一定能顺利举办，到时候我们再一起庆祝吧。 | 两个样例均使用本版本的 `scripts/run_tangyuge_infer.py`，以随机种子 9001 生成。 ### 仓库结构 ```text ├── README.md ├── LICENSE # Apache-2.0 ├── THIRD_PARTY.md # 随附第三方模型的来源 ├── weights/ # 微调权重（fp16） │ ├── tangyuge_v2pp_dpo-e10.ckpt # GPT（文本 -> 语义 token） │ └── tangyuge_v2pp_e4_s564.pth # SoVITS（语义 token -> 波形） ├── GPT-SoVITS-overlay/ # 辅助模型 + 基础模型，目录结构与 GPT-SoVITS 相同 ├── configs/tts_infer_pack.yaml # GPT-SoVITS 推理配置 ├── profiles/ # 19 个场景配置 ├── references/ # 19 个场景参考音频 ├── samples/ # 输出样例 ├── scripts/ # 安装 / 推理 / HTTP 桥接脚本、GPT 学习率调度启动器 ├── assets/ # 本模型卡使用的图表 └── manifests/ ├── references.yaml # 参考音频 <-> 提示文本绑定关系 ├── training_report.md # 完整训练与评测报告（中文） └── checksums.sha256 # 文件哈希 ``` ## 训练详情 ### 训练数据 所有声音数据均来自该角色的游戏内台词（从游戏提取的 702 条音频，约 48.8 分钟）；数据集本身**不**公开。转写文本已通过 ASR 检查：未发现明显错误的标注（平均拼音错误率为 2.0%，没有超过 30% 的样本）。 | 阶段 | 数据 | | --- | --- | | SoVITS | 561 条真实录音（1–12 s，至少 6 个汉字），约 43.1 分钟 | | GPT | 1559 条音频：**685 条真实录音**（上述 561 条 + 因时长和字数规则而被剔除的 124 条短句 / 感叹词台词；仅用于 GPT）、**845 条合成音频**（约 57.5 分钟；由商业 TTS 服务模仿同一声音生成，按下述条件筛选），以及 **29 条重复加入的**含有“我们”的真实录音 | 合成数据筛选（以下均为机器门槛）：时长 1–12 s、削波比例 ≤ 1%、相对于本地 Paraformer 转写结果的文本拼音编辑距离 ≤ 1（不超过 4 个音节的台词要求为 0）且覆盖率 ≥ 0.9、DNSMOS 背景评分 ≥ 3.5；对于笑声台词，带事件标签的语音转写结果中必须出现对应事件标签。合成部分中包含“我们”的音频均被剔除（其发音与真实声音不匹配），维护者还通过试听剔除了 5 条听感不自然的音频。 ### 训练流程 **SoVITS**（与首版相同）：从 `s2Gv2ProPlus.pth` / `s2Dv2ProPlus.pth` 开始训练，批大小为 4，学习率为 1e-4，采用 fp16，保存了 8 轮，最终选择第 4 轮（第 564 步）。 **GPT**（本版本）：从官方 `s1v3.ckpt` 开始，使用官方训练脚本和优化器（ScaledAdam，每 4 个批次执行一次优化器更新），批大小为 4，16 位混合精度，共 10 轮，每轮保存一个检查点。 - *学习率。* 上游代码将 GPT 学习率固定为常数 0.002，因此每轮保存的检查点都是高学习率下的快照，拼音错误率在不同轮次之间波动（我们的训练中为 1.5–4.7%）。我们仅替换了调度器，通过启动器实现，未修改 GPT-SoVITS 源码（`scripts/s1_train_annealed.py`，总更新次数通过 `S1_TOTAL_UPDATES` 环境变量设置）：先线性预热（在 50 次优化器更新内从 1e-5 升至 2e-3），再余弦衰减至 1e-4。使用该调度后，各轮之间的波动降至 1.25–1.63%。 - *DPO。* 官方“DPO 训练（实验性）”选项（s1 配置中的 `train.if_dpo: true`）会添加一项偏好损失（β = 0.2，无参考模型）：对每个批次，通过重复或删除一个随机片段构造“被拒绝”的语义序列，使模型学会减少重复音节和吞音节。 - *观察。* DPO 训练日志中的步数是非 DPO 训练的两倍（7769 对比 3889），学习率约在第 6 轮而非第 10 轮降至下限，原因是总更新次数（970）按非 DPO 训练设置。因此第 7–10 轮均在最低学习率 1e-4 下运行。我们没有测试重新按比例调整的调度。 比较的变体（均从 `s1v3.ckpt` 开始）：`F` / `F2`（恒定学习率，14 轮；F2 剔除了含“我们”的合成音频）、`G-F` / `G-F2`（相同数据，退火学习率，10 轮），以及最终发布的 **`G-F2+DPO`**（G-F2 加上官方 DPO，10 轮）。 ![GPT 训练曲线](assets/01_gpt_training_curves.png) *训练 top-3 准确率越高，意味着记忆程度越强；未使用退火的训练持续上升至 0.79，而使用退火的训练最终约为 0.60。DPO 训练的损失包含偏好项，因此未绘制。* 我们还重新训练了 SoVITS（真实录音 + 合成数据，从官方基础模型开始，共 6 轮），但未采用其结果：见[评测](#evaluation)。其日志损失为每 100 步记录一次的单批次值，噪声过大，难以解读；只有 KL 项呈下降趋势。 ![SoVITS 重新训练曲线](assets/02_sovits_training_curves.png) ### 计算资源 一张 RTX 4060 Laptop（8 GB）。DPO GPT 训练（10 轮）耗时约 24 分钟，批大小为 4 时占用约 6.4 GB 显存；SoVITS 每轮约需 2–5.5 分钟，取决于数据规模。 ## 评测 ### 评测方案 候选模型与基线使用相同句子、相同参考音频和相同随机种子进行比较；所有图表均展示配对差值，以及按句子进行 bootstrap 重采样所得的 95% 区间。 - **测试句子：** 100 个未出现在训练数据中的句子（已与台词脚本核对）；另加 12 句（6 句笑声、6 句感叹词）；最终检查另用 **59 个未见句子**（已与训练台词脚本及此前全部测试句子核对，额外加入笑声、叹气和情感台词）。 - **参考音频：** 两个真实声音的场景参考（`serious_script41_L0682`、`question_clear_script34_L0420`）；根据测试集不同，每句使用 1–3 个随机种子。 - **指标** - *拼音错误率（PER）：* 目标文本与本地 Paraformer-large 转写结果之间的不带声调拼音编辑距离；不计笑声台词。*严重错误率：* PER > 10% 的语句占比。 - *说话人相似度：* 相对于真实录音的 ERes2NetV2 嵌入余弦相似度。 - *DNSMOS（P.835）：* SIG（语音失真）、BAK（背景噪声）；*底噪：* 非静音帧 RMS 的第 10 百分位数（dB）。 - *事件召回率：* 对于同文本参考演绎中包含非语音事件（笑声、吸气、叹气）的句子，支持事件标签的语音转写服务在我们的输出中检测到的对应事件类型所占比例（此类句子共 13–16 个，使用一个参考）。 - *韵律接近度：* 相对于该参考演绎的 log-F0 和能量轮廓相关性，以及语速比（区分系统的能力较弱；各版本差异约为 0.01）。 - **综合评分与门槛**（用于选择检查点）：说话人相似度占 35%、情感 / 非语音事件占 25%、发音占 25%、干净度占 15%。每项配对差值线性映射至 0–100（50 表示与基线相同）。首先应用三项门槛：说话人相似度下降不超过 0.01、PER 上升不超过 0.3 个百分点、严重错误率上升不超过 1.5 个百分点。 ### 结果 最终比较采用 59 个未见句子 × 2 个参考音频 × 3 个随机种子（每个系统 354 条语音）： | 指标 | e14（首版） | d2（上一版） | **本版本** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 拼音错误率（不计笑声台词） | 4.42% | 2.41% | 2.53% | | 严重错误率（PER > 10%） | 13.0% | 10.3% | 11.0% | | 事件召回率（笑声 / 吸气 / 叹气） | 0.67 | 0.58 | **0.77** | | 说话人相似度 | 0.884 | 0.886 | 0.885 | | DNSMOS SIG / BAK | 3.13 / 3.66 | 3.10 / 3.61 | 3.12 / 3.58 | | 底噪（dB） | −57.2 | −56.7 | −56.6 | ![版本对比](assets/04_final_vs_previous.png) 汇总全部测试数据后的综合分：相对于 d2 为 **57.4**（95% 区间 48.2–67.3；119 个句子，474 对），相对于 e14 为 **66.8**（51.4–73.6；159 个句子，554 对）；三项门槛均通过。 **如何解读。** 发音、音色和干净度与 d2 持平；明显差异是笑声 / 吸气 / 叹气提示的呈现率提高了约 0.2。每项指标的区间均有重叠，因此应理解为“没有变差，且更擅长非语音事件”，而非所有方面均有统计显著的提升。PER 绝对值高度依赖句子集（简短感叹词台词较难），不能与使用其他句子集的早期报告直接比较。 各轮表现（100 个句子 × 2 个参考音频，一个随机种子，相对于 e14）： ![各轮对比](assets/03_gpt_epoch_comparison.png) - `G-F2+DPO`：全部 10 轮均通过门槛，每轮发音均优于 e14，事件召回率保持在 0.62–0.84。第 2–10 轮形成平台期（综合分 59–68）。第 6 轮和第 10 轮在未见句子及新随机种子上复测，第 10 轮在汇总数据中得分更高，因此选择发布该轮。第 2 轮在首个测试集上得分最高，但在未见句子上有所回落。 - `G-F2`（无 DPO）：从第 6 轮起，事件召回率降至 0.47–0.53，并且在未见句子上未通过严重错误率门槛。`G-F` 的事件召回率为 0.53–0.72，未在未见句子上复测。 - `F` / `F2`（恒定学习率）：各轮之间波动较大。 重新训练的 SoVITS **未能**优于随仓库发布的第 4 轮：汇总两个随机种子（424 对）后，最佳候选相对于 50 分基线的得分为 54.1（95% 区间 44.7–62.7）和 51.9（44.6–61.6）；与新 GPT 搭配后，结果有好有坏（52.7 和 44.5）。因此 SoVITS 保持不变。 ![选择结果汇总](assets/05_selection_forest.png) ### 本次评测的局限 仅使用两个真实参考音频；事件召回率的句子集较小；韵律指标几乎无法区分系统；综合评分权重依赖主观判断；自动指标无法检测上述电音伪影。维护者还试听了 30 条随机抽取的输出（分层随机抽取的 10 个未见句子 × 3 个随机种子），并据此接受了发布版本。 ## 技术规格 - **GPT：** 基于语义 token 的自回归 transformer 解码器，24 层、隐藏维度 512、16 个注意力头、前馈层维度 2048、语义词表大小 1025（1024 + EOS）、音素词表大小 732，BERT 特征来自 `chinese-roberta-wwm-ext-large`，训练音频最长 54 s。 - **SoVITS（v2ProPlus）：** VITS 风格生成器，以参考音频和说话人验证嵌入（ERes2NetV2 `sv/` 模型）为条件解码语义 token；输出为 32 kHz。 - **软件：** GPT-SoVITS `ea2d2a8`、Python 3.10、PyTorch 2.4.0（CUDA 12.4）。**硬件：** 推荐 NVIDIA GPU；CPU 注意事项见上文。 ## 许可与权利 本仓库以 # qwen3-tts-0.6b-base-ov

OpenVINO IR export of [Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base), split for **round-based continuous batching** — many synthesis requests share one GPU, each advancing one 80 ms frame per round. Built and validated on an Intel Arc B580 with OpenVINO 2026.4.1.

Same layout, conversion recipe and runtime notes as [jinhwan000/qwen3-tts-1.7b-base-ov](https://huggingface.co/jinhwan000/qwen3-tts-1.7b-base-ov) — see that card for what each part is, how it must be loaded (PagedAttention conversion of `talker.xml` and `dec_transformer.xml` with `sliding_window` = 72, static buckets for `frame_head.xml` and `dec_back.xml`) and the B580 precision settings (f16, KV f16, frame head `ACTIVATIONS_SCALE_FACTOR=8`). Sibling: [qwen3-tts-0.6b-customvoice-ov](https://huggingface.co/jinhwan000/qwen3-tts-0.6b-customvoice-ov).

> **Sentence-end cut-off.** In our tests this model often ends an utterance in the middle of its last syllable (the talker emits EOS early): 5–6 of 8 Korean utterances, and 22 % of the official fp32 reference outputs as well — it is the model's behaviour, not the export's. The 1.7B Base model does not show it to the same degree, and the 0.6B CustomVoice model does not show it.

Differences from the 1.7B export: talker hidden 1024 (28 layers, attention 16 × 128 = 2048 wide, 8 KV heads), so `talker.xml` inputs are [t, 1024] and `text_proj.xml` maps [t, 2048] → [t, 1024]; the speaker encoder in `model.safetensors` gives a 1024-dimensional x-vector. The speech decoder parts (`dec_transformer`, `dec_back`, `decoder_host.safetensors`) are the same as in the 1.7B export.

The IR covers only the model parts. Also needed from the original repository: `model.safetensors`, `config.json`, `generation_config.json`, `vocab.json`, `merges.txt`, `tokenizer_config.json` and `speech_tokenizer/config.json`.

## Validation (Arc B580, OpenVINO 2026.4.1)

Forced-input parity against the official fp32 reference (4 Korean cases, 54–108 frames, greedy):

| device | talker hidden (relative RMS) | greedy codes vs reference (c0 · code predictor) | decode SNR vs official decoder |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU f32 | 1.2e-6 | 100 % · 100 % | 110.5–112.8 dB |
| Arc B580 f16 | 1.7–2.2e-3 | 99.1–100 % · 98.0–99.1 % | 51.7–53.2 dB |

Round-batched synthesis on the Arc B580 (every request synthesising non-stop, 10 s per point):

| active requests | round median · p95 | rounds > 80 ms | per-utterance RTF (median) | first audio frame (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 24.4 · 29.4 ms | 0 % | 0.32 | 49 ms |
| 32 | 48.7 · 58.8 ms | 0 % | 0.59 | 94 ms |
| 64 | 64.5 · 72.7 ms | 0 % | 0.82 | 122 ms |

(talker · frame head · decoder per round at 64 requests: 21.0 · 22.5 · 19.9 ms. RTF = generation time ÷ audio length.) 64 concurrent requests is the real-time limit we use on the B580 for this model. Only Korean was validated here; the parts are language-independent.

Apache-2.0, following the upstream model.

# Chatterbox Multilingual: Brazilian Portuguese (MLX)

Converted from [ResembleAI/Chatterbox-Multilingual-pt-br](https://huggingface.co/ResembleAI/Chatterbox-Multilingual-pt-br) using
mlx-audio 0.6.1. Source precision is preserved;
weights are **not quantized**. The V3 Brazilian Portuguese T3, speech decoder,
and tokenizer come from the source repository. The voice encoder and Cangjie
mapping come from ResembleAI/chatterbox. Exact revisions are recorded in conversion.json.

Use an Apple Silicon Mac with the mlx-audio version from the accompanying
conversion script's requirements. Supply a reference voice recording:

## Required runtime fix for distorted audio

The converter's MLX-Audio version uses a final HiFT activation slope of 0.1,
where the official PyTorch decoder uses 0.01. This causes clipping and harsh
distortion with these weights. Apply the included patch in your inference
Python environment, then restart any process that already loaded the decoder:

```bash
hf download theoracleguy/Chatterbox-Multilingual-pt-br-MLX patch_chatterbox_vocoder.py --local-dir ./chatterbox-runtime-fix
python ./chatterbox-runtime-fix/patch_chatterbox_vocoder.py
```

For OpenVox, apply the patch to the hifigan.py file in the app's bundled runtime
source, then rebuild and relaunch. Patching a separate Python venv does not
change an already-running app. The model weights do not need reconversion.

On identical mel/source inputs, the patched MLX vocoder matched the official
PyTorch output within 1.1e-6 RMS error on the diagnostic sample, with no samples
at amplitude >=0.98 (versus 14.0% before the fix).

## Generate speech

```bash
mlx_audio.tts.generate --model theoracleguy/Chatterbox-Multilingual-pt-br-MLX --text "Olá! Como você está?" --lang_code pt --ref_audio reference.wav
```

The shared speech tokenizer, mlx-community/S3TokenizerV2, is downloaded
automatically during inference. Language code: `pt` (locale: pt-BR).
Conversion validates component weights. The vocoder fix has been checked
against official PyTorch output; a broad listening evaluation is still pending.

# VoxCPM2 - BFloat16 (full precision)

MLX port of [openbmb/VoxCPM2](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/VoxCPM2) — a 2B-parameter multilingual TTS model with 48kHz studio-quality output, voice cloning, and voice design.

Full precision BFloat16 weights. Best quality, largest size.

## Features
- **30 languages** — including English, Chinese, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, and more
- **48kHz output** — studio-quality audio
- **Voice Design** — create voices from text descriptions (no reference audio needed)
- **Voice Cloning** — clone any voice from a short audio reference
- **4 generation modes** — zero-shot, continuation, reference cloning, combined

## Usage

```bash
pip install mlx-audio

# Zero-shot
python -m mlx_audio.tts.generate --model mlx-community/VoxCPM2-bf16 --text "Hello world" --verbose

# Voice design
python -m mlx_audio.tts.generate --model mlx-community/VoxCPM2-bf16 \
  --text "Hello world" \
  --instruct "A young woman, gentle and sweet voice"

# Voice cloning
python -m mlx_audio.tts.generate --model mlx-community/VoxCPM2-bf16 \
  --text "Hello world" \
  --ref_audio speaker.wav --ref_text "reference text"
```

### Python API

```python
from mlx_audio.tts import load_model

model = load_model("mlx-community/VoxCPM2-bf16")

# Generate
for result in model.generate(
    text="Hello, this is VoxCPM2 on Apple Silicon.",
    inference_timesteps=7,
    cfg_value=2.0,
):
    print(f"Duration: {result.audio_duration}")
```

## Performance (Apple Silicon)

| Variant | Size | RTF (7 timesteps) |
|---------|------|--------------------|
| bf16 | 4.96 GB | 0.48x |
| **8-bit** | **3.23 GB** | **0.85x** |
| **4-bit** | **2.30 GB** | **0.90x** |

*RTF = Real-Time Factor (>1.0 = faster than realtime)*

## Original Model
- [openbmb/VoxCPM2](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/VoxCPM2)
- Apache 2.0 License

Converted with [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio).
