# qwen3-tts-1.7b-base-ov

OpenVINO IR export of [Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base), split for **round-based continuous batching** — many synthesis requests share one GPU, each advancing one 80 ms frame per round. Built and validated on an Intel Arc B580 with OpenVINO 2026.4.1.

This is **not** an optimum-intel / OpenVINO GenAI export. The parts are driven by a small C++ shim (OpenVINO C++ API) and a C# round scheduler: the talker and the speech-decoder transformer are converted to PagedAttention at load time, and the frame head and decoder back half are compiled once per static request-count bucket. Same family: [qwen3-tts-0.6b-base-ov](https://huggingface.co/jinhwan000/qwen3-tts-0.6b-base-ov) · [qwen3-tts-0.6b-customvoice-ov](https://huggingface.co/jinhwan000/qwen3-tts-0.6b-customvoice-ov).

## Parts (`ov/`)

| file | what | shapes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `talker.xml` | talker body (28 layers + final norm), **stateful-LM shaped** — apply `SDPAToPagedAttention` on load (C++ API only; the converted model cannot be re-read from a file) | `inputs_embeds` [t, 2048] → hidden of each sequence's last row |
| `text_proj.xml` | text_projection MLP | text-embedding rows [t, 2048] → [t, 2048] |
| `frame_head.xml` | codec head + codebook-0 sampling (repetition-penalty mask, EOS rule, top-k 50, inverse CDF) + 15 code-predictor steps unrolled + next talker row | `hidden` [n, 2048], `uniforms` [n, 16], `penalty` [n, 3072], `eos_rule` [n], `forced` [n, 16], `text_row` [n, 2048] → `codes` [n, 16], `eos` [n], `next_row` [n, 2048]; dynamic n — reshape to static buckets |
| `dec_transformer.xml` | speech-decoder pre_conv (folded into a Linear over [x(t−2), x(t−1), x(t)]) + 8-layer transformer, stateful — convert to PagedAttention and set `sliding_window` = 72 (PagedAttention input 10; 72 = window including the current frame) | [t, 1536] → [t, 1024] |
| `dec_back.xml` | decoder upsampling + conv blocks for one frame per request; conv tails and transposed-conv spill carried as explicit `state_i` → `new_state_i` (20 tensors, 140,448 values per request) | `x` [n, 1024] + states → `pcm` [n, 1920] (24 kHz) |
| `decoder_host.safetensors` | `rvq_table` [16, 2048, 512] f32 — codebooks with the output projection folded in; the host sums 16 rows per frame | |
| `ov.json` | dimensions and decoder state shapes | |

Weights are stored in f32; the device precision hint decides how they run. On the Arc B580: `INFERENCE_PRECISION_HINT=f16` and `KV_CACHE_PRECISION=f16` for the paged parts, and **`ACTIVATIONS_SCALE_FACTOR=8` for the frame head** — without it the code-predictor MLP overflows f16 (gate·up products reach ~170,000) and the predicted codes are silently wrong. f32 does not compile on the B580 (`CL_BUILD_PROGRAM_FAILURE`); CPU runs f32.

The decoder's Snake activation is written as `x + c − c·cos(2a·x)` (c = b/2) — the same value as `x + b·sin²(a·x)`, but the `Power(·, 2)` of the direct form runs as a generic pow on the GPU and made Snake (~58 % of the decoder back half) almost twice as slow.

The IR covers only the model parts. Also needed from the original repository: `model.safetensors` (codec / text embedding tables read on the host, and the speaker encoder for x-vector voice clones), `config.json`, `generation_config.json`, `vocab.json`, `merges.txt`, `tokenizer_config.json` and `speech_tokenizer/config.json`.

## Validation (Arc B580, OpenVINO 2026.4.1)

Forced-input parity against the official fp32 reference (4 Korean cases, 61–103 frames, greedy):

| device | talker hidden (relative RMS) | greedy codes vs reference (c0 · code predictor) | decode SNR vs official decoder |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU f32 | 1.2e-6 | 100 % · 100 % | 110–112 dB |
| Arc B580 f16 | 1.9–2.7e-3 (bf16 CUDA: 4.2–5.5e-3) | 100 % · 98.9–99.1 % | 50.3–52.8 dB |

Round-batched synthesis on the Arc B580 (every request synthesising non-stop, 10 s per point; a request needs one 80 ms frame per round to stay real time):

| active requests | round median · p95 | rounds > 80 ms | per-utterance RTF (median) | first audio frame (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 28.7 · 37.9 ms | 0 % | 0.44 | 47 ms |
| 16 | 37.5 · 53.1 ms | 0.4 % | 0.52 | 86 ms |
| 48 | 58.0 · 70.3 ms | 1.8 % | 0.76 | 119 ms |

(talker · frame head · decoder per round at 48 requests: 20.2 · 20.9 · 16.9 ms. RTF = generation time ÷ audio length.)

48 concurrent requests is the real-time saturation point of the B580 (compute at ~99 %); with 48 slots the device memory is about 9.9 GB. First start compiles every bucket (about 35 s on the B580); with an OpenVINO compile cache later starts take a few seconds plus a ~7 s warm-up. Only Korean was validated here; the parts are language-independent.

# mlx-community/chatterbox-multilingual-v3

This is Chatterbox Multilingual V3, converted to MLX format from [ResembleAI/chatterbox](https://huggingface.co/ResembleAI/chatterbox) using [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) version **0.4.7**.

**Note:** This model requires the S3Tokenizer weights from [mlx-community/S3TokenizerV2](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/S3TokenizerV2), which will be downloaded automatically.

## Use with mlx-audio

```bash
pip install -U mlx-audio
```

### Command line

```bash
mlx_audio.tts.generate --model mlx-community/chatterbox-multilingual-v3 --text "Bonjour, voici Chatterbox sur MLX !" --ref_audio reference.wav --lang_code fr
```

### Python

```python
from mlx_audio.tts.generate import generate_audio

generate_audio(
    text="Bonjour, voici Chatterbox sur MLX !",
    model="mlx-community/chatterbox-multilingual-v3",
    ref_audio="reference.wav",
    lang_code="fr",
    file_prefix="output",
)
```
